headline: Transcriptomic and multi-omics models yield prognostic signatures in diverse cancers
label: Multi Omics Cancer Transcriptomic Modeling
summary: Public bulk, single-cell and multi-omics cohorts are combined to derive prognostic signatures and immune-landscape readouts across cancer types.
synthesis: The common thread is cohort-level transcriptomic and multi-omics profiling used to derive prognostic signatures and characterize tumor immune microenvironments. Many items build risk scores or biomarker panels from public cohorts such as TCGA and GEO, often pairing bulk data with scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics to localize the signal: a 15-gene PTM risk score in melanoma, an eight-gene T cell RiskScore in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, and a seven-gene mitochondrial RNA modification model in colorectal cancer. The ovarian preprint details an interpretable three-stage ML framework over TCGA multi-omics that yields a 20-biomarker macrophage/complement survival signature. Some studies extend toward genetic or circulating readouts, including Mendelian randomization for FAM174B in COPD and lung adenocarcinoma and a circulating three-miRNA panel for early ovarian cancer. The set is heterogeneous; the small-cohort pancreatic ML study with an unvalidated four-gene panel remains exploratory.
